call.sequence_note: The rep references a previous attempt to connect — 'Like I said last time was just a little bit annoying, but we were able to jump on' — which reads as a failed or aborted earlier meeting rather than a completed prior sales call. All discovery is run fresh here, so treat this as the first substantive conversation.

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter named on the call. The prospect describes finding the programme himself via Instagram and booking directly: 'this is why I decided to reach out to you guys' and 'what sort of got you to actually book a meeting with me in the first place'.

prospect.name: Ali
prospect.occupation: Manages a group of companies employing roughly 400 people
prospect.family_status: Father of two children, aged two and four
prospect.training_background: Lifelong exerciser; describes training as part of his identity. Cycles through online fitness programmes roughly every four months, trains consistently in blocks of one to one and a half months before questioning the method. Plays golf three times a week. Has taken mobility classes and rates his own mobility as very good. Minimal kettlebell exposure — 'I did some kettlebell at the gym, but never too much, just one exercise'.

signals: Already lean and trained: self-reports 11-12% body fat, visible abs confirmed on camera, 80 kg at 1.81-1.82 m
Explicitly framing this as good-to-great: 'I really want to take everything to a higher level... I want to go a step above'
Successful operator: 'I manage a big group of companies for almost 400 people'

Price is a deliberation, not a barrier — asked whether it is affordable, he answered 'No, no, it's possible' and reframed it as business discipline: 'It's not because you have money that you just throw money around'
Aspiration is aesthetic refinement, not rescue: 'the perfect body... it's Brad Pitt in Fight Club'

goals.text: Get leaner while keeping muscle volume — from a two-to-four-pack to a full six-pack
Maintain and further improve already-good mobility
Finally understand his own macros and nutrition with confirmation from an expert rather than from videos
Learn a protocol he can run independently after the six months rather than depending on a coach
Train effectively in three to four sessions a week around a demanding job, two small children and golf
Protect his back so he can keep playing golf — 'your back is very important for all sports, but also for golf and for life'
Keep raising his own ceiling because improving is who he is — 'it's my way of not getting bored'

pains.text: Never reaches the peak he is chasing — 'each time when summer comes, I train during two, three, four months... but I never kind of reach that little extra mile that I want in terms of body fat percentage'
Breaks his own consistency by second-guessing the method — 'I'm gonna train for one month non-stop, and then I'm gonna say, okay, am I tracking my macros well? I'm starting questioning the method'
No authoritative nutrition guidance; has self-taught from videos and chased trends — 'at some point it was BCAA, before that it was protein powder'
Very busy schedule across a large business and two young children, competing with golf and training time
Worry about injuring his back through poor kettlebell technique — 'if you don't do it, you can injure yourself'
Age-related caution about what supplements and methods are still appropriate — 'I'm 41, I'm not like 30 or 20, so you need to make sure that you're doing stuff that are also healthy'

objections.raw_quote: to be completely transparent with you, I only have one concern, you know, about the training is that I know that you really have to execute well the movements, and because, you know, the back, if you don't do it, you can injure yourself
objections.rep_response: Explained Trevor's video-feedback loop, that he would start on lower weight to build the foundation over one to two months, and turned it into a commitment question: 'are you going to communicate these things with him, so he can actually intervene?'

objections.raw_quote: the first thing is about the trust, you know, because of course, you know, if you wire just, you know, this amount, you're not sure, you know, who you are working with
objections.rep_response: Did not address trust directly. Answered it commercially by inventing a $1,200 one-month trial with an exit — 'if at the end you feel like I don't really love it, then we'll leave it there'.

objections.raw_quote: well, if you can give me some time to sleep on it, you know, think about it, you know, this evening, and then I will give you my answer probably tomorrow
objections.rep_response: Asked for his gut feeling, asked whether he wants it overall, asked whether reaching the peak is worth 6K, isolated the hesitation down to the investment amount, then accepted the delay and booked a phone call for 7pm the next day.

objections.raw_quote: I need to think about it also to, you know, I mean, to discuss it, you know, with the, with my family
objections.rep_response: Did not acknowledge or address it at all; carried on isolating the money objection.

objections.raw_quote: the cost is also something that I need to take into account because it's not a small investment money-wise, I would say, not time-wise, for anyone
objections.rep_response: Asked whether the peak is worth 6K, then established the money is available rather than absent — 'is it just a high amount that you have to invest in yourself... or is it more so that it's just not possible?' — answer: 'No, no, it's possible.' Then argued that decisive business people get the best results.

objections.raw_quote: if you have other alternatives, you need to compare them and then decide based on the different options and also based on the success rate of each option
objections.rep_response: Probed whether he had specific alternatives in mind (he did not), then narrowed it to 'the only reason that you will be looking into doing something else potentially comes down to the investments', which the prospect confirmed.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Improvised on the call. A $1,200 first month framed as a trial, then either $4,800 at the end of that month with no interest, or three payments with no interest, or six payments which 'would add interest per month' — the interest rate was never stated. The rep was unsure of his own numbers: 'Then I don't know the exact amount, I think that's just around 1,200.' The trial carries an explicit exit: 'if you feel like I don't really love it, then we'll leave it there.'

evidence: Explicitly deferred: 'if you can give me some time to sleep on it... I will give you my answer probably tomorrow'
No payment taken and no payment link sent
A specific callback was agreed — a WhatsApp phone call at 7pm local the following day

Positive counter-signal: he confirmed intent and affordability, 'it's worth it because health is very important for me' and 'No, no, it's possible', and said of the plan 'I think that that will be my preferred method right now'

Negative counter-signal: his answer to the commitment check was hedged — 'Hopefully, you know, like we say here in Morocco, we will do all the efforts and then if God wants' — and the rep moved to price on that hedge
He also introduced a family discussion late in the call, which was never addressed
outcome.next_step: WhatsApp phone call at 7pm Morocco time the following day for his decision.

notable.note: A near-textbook ICP prospect — 41, runs a 400-person group, 11-12% body fat, affordability confirmed — was taken to a hedge rather than a yes, and the rep responded to a trust objection by inventing a commercial structure that does not exist in the offer: a $1,200 one-month trial with a walk-away, and instalment options where six payments carry unspecified interest and three do not. The rep also did not know his own numbers mid-quote. Separately, the prospect said he wanted to discuss it with his family and that was never acknowledged, and the rep applied light social pressure by contrasting him with business people who 'just do it'.

quality.notes: Frequent inversion of short and medium turns throughout. Clear examples: the rep's own questions appear under 'Ali' at 00:02:43 ('So you want to get even leaner?'), 00:13:42 ('Why do you want to go to that next level?') and 00:39:06 (the interest-terms explanation), while the prospect's answers appear under the rep's label at 00:07:04 and 00:09:50. Roles were resolved from content throughout. Several passages are also garbled by transcription ('apps' for 'abs', 'diastetics' for 'aesthetics', 'Guter' inserted repeatedly).
